title: Top-action-weighted source-KL temperature smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Applying a lower temperature only inside the Standard10 source-KL loss will better preserve the mature reference's greedy top-action ordering while leaving rollout and PPO sampling at T=1, improving a matched three-anchor greedy panel over ordinary source-KL.
material_change: Add an independently configurable source-policy KL temperature with exact inherit-by-default compatibility. Reuse the audited ordinary source-KL T=1 control; train one fresh Standard10-start treatment on the identical seed, fixed deals, adaptive three-policy league, optimizer, and about 10k physical-hand boundary, changing only source-KL temperature from 1 to 0.5. Evaluate on untouched common decks; no Slumbot.
baseline: Ordinary source-KL control from v6-greedy-advantage-margin-smoke; direct current-greedy margin, source-greedy margin, and hero/PPO low temperature all failed scale gates. Standard10 greedy historical fresh20k remains -11.4275 bb/100 CI[-28.7124,5.8574]; single imitation-teacher fresh20k -18.5025 is negative evidence.

result.summary: A source-KL-only temperature of 0.5, with hero rollout/PPO held at T=1, completed 10,407 new physical hands and a raw-audited common-deck three-anchor smoke.
result.conclusion: Treatment-control pooled +12.492839 bb/100 with paired 95% CI [-3.865282,28.850959], 2/3 positive anchors. Crucially Standard10 was +19.907227 rather than the negative direction seen with hero low temperature. Training iteration1 assignments matched exactly; adaptive iteration2 assignments diverged under asynchronous outcomes, while seeds and pool identities remained fixed.
result.next_step: Run fresh matched T1 versus source-KL-T0.5 arms to about 65k physical hands per arm with fixed seeds/deals and a new untouched multi-anchor endpoint gate. Do not spend Slumbot unless the longer-horizon gate passes.
